# Gas appliances and gas lines

Notes from the utility's safety flyer and our plumber.

## If you smell gas

Natural gas is given a rotten-egg odor so leaks can be noticed. If you smell it, do not switch lights or appliances on or off, do not light anything, and do not use a phone inside. Get everyone out, leave the door open, and call the gas company's emergency number or 911 from outside or a neighbor's house. Do not go back until the utility says it is safe.

## Gas line work needs a permit

Adding or moving a gas line, such as for a new range or a grill hookup, must be done by a licensed plumber or gas fitter under a permit. The line is pressure-tested and inspected before it is covered. Replace flexible appliance connectors older than 10 years.

## Pilot lights and carbon monoxide

A gas flame should burn blue; yellow or orange flames and soot mean incomplete combustion and carbon monoxide. Put a CO alarm on every level and outside each sleeping area. If the alarm goes off, go outside and call 911.

## Annual service

Have the furnace and water heater serviced every year. Keep the area around them clear, and never store paint thinner or gasoline near a gas appliance.
